categories.name: Health
categories.description:
Population and individual health indicators — mental health, substance
use, mortality, life quality, healthcare contact. Most sources are FHI
Folkehelsestatistikk tables with 3-year rolling averages.

categories.name: Demographics
categories.description:
Population structure by age, sex, kommune, and bydel. Core denominators
for any rate-based analysis. Includes SSB resident counts and FHI
population projections.

categories.name: Income & poverty
categories.description:
Household income, low-income statistics, persistent low income, and
children in low-income households. SSB EU-SILC-derived series plus
Bufdir's child-poverty kommunemonitor.

categories.name: Education & youth
categories.description:
Educational outcomes — upper-secondary completion, NEET status,
educational attainment by region. Includes bullying and youth wellbeing
indicators that intersect with school context.

categories.name: Social & housing
categories.description:
Social assistance use, household composition, overcrowded housing,
and integration indicators. The bridge between need and the services
that respond to it.

categories.name: NGO supply
categories.description:
Norwegian NGO supply data — chapters, activities, and operational
footprint across the civil-society sector. Pairs with the population
and need indicators to surface coverage gaps.

categories.name: Organisations register
categories.description:
The Norwegian register of legal entities — Brønnøysundregistrene's
Enhetsregisteret, held in full. Not an indicator: it is the population
of organisations that every other NGO and sector question is asked
about, and the join target for organisasjonsnummer.

categories.name: Reference geographies
categories.description:
Canonical geographic dimensions used as join keys across every
indicator: kommune and fylke classifications from SSB Klass.

publishers.notes:
The Brønnøysund Register Centre — the Norwegian government agency that
operates the country's central registers. Atlas reads Enhetsregisteret
(every registered legal entity, ~1.17M) and Frivillighetsregisteret (the
voluntary-organisation register, a filtered view of the same entities).
Data released under NLOD 2.0; `organisasjonsnummer` is the join key that
makes organisational data from any Norwegian source line up.

No logo: Brreg's mark is not offered under the same open licence as the
data, so the publisher page renders without one rather than
redistributing it.

Directorate for Children, Youth and Family Affairs. Publishes the
Barnefattigdom kommunemonitor and related family / child-welfare
indicators at kommune and bydel resolution. Data released under NLOD.

Norwegian Institute of Public Health. Publishes the Folkehelseprofiler
and the underlying Folkehelsestatistikk via statistikk.fhi.no.
Most tables use 3-year rolling averages and standardised ratios (SMR)
to compare kommune-level health outcomes.

Norwegian Red Cross. Source of NGO-supply data via the public
Organizations API (branches and per-branch activities).

Norway's national statistics office. Maintains the StatBank
(statistikkbanken) — the canonical source of demographic, economic,
and social indicators at kommune, fylke, and national resolution.
Data released under NLOD; tables identified by numeric IDs preserved
with leading zeros (e.g. table 07459).

sources.description:
Brønnøysundregistrene's Enhetsregisteret holds every legal entity registered in
Norway — companies, foundations, associations, public bodies and sole
proprietorships — around 1.17 million of them. Brreg regenerates a complete
gzipped JSON export daily; Atlas downloads that file, streams it, and stores each
record verbatim as jsonb in `raw.brreg_enheter_snapshot`, keyed on
organisasjonsnummer.

Atlas previously held 122 organisational units, selected by a curated list of 11
NGOs. Holding the whole register instead means any Norwegian organisation can be
resolved from its organisasjonsnummer without a new ingest, and it is what makes
organisational data from unrelated sources join at all.

This is the **bootstrap** load: a complete point-in-time copy. Keeping it current
is the change feed's job (PLAN-002, `/oppdateringer/enheter`), which reads only
what moved. Underenheter (~863k sub-units) are a separate follow-on.

Nothing is flattened, renamed or re-encoded on the way in. Typed columns for the
fields Atlas actually queries are built in dbt (PLAN-003).
sources.attribution: Inneholder data under norsk lisens for offentlige data (NLOD) tilgjengeliggjort av Brønnøysundregistrene
sources.methodology_notes:
Source file: GET https://data.brreg.no/enhetsregisteret/api/enheter/lastned —
one gzipped, pretty-printed JSON array, regenerated daily. Measured 2026-09-11:
210,132,682 bytes compressed, 2,005,028,121 uncompressed, 1,173,878 records.

It is not newline-delimited, so the loader streams it with a depth-aware scanner
and parses one element at a time; the whole register loads in ~33 MB of resident
memory.

🔴 One thing this load deliberately does not do. The reference implementation
(terchris/shadow-brreg) converted the JSON to pipe-delimited CSV and stripped
every `|` from the source first, so any organisation with a pipe in its name or
address was silently altered. There is no delimited format anywhere in Atlas's
path, and a test asserts a record containing a pipe, a newline and a double quote
survives byte-identical.

The bulk file and the live API do not agree exactly: on 2026-09-11 the file held
1,173,878 records against the API's 1,174,098 — a 220-record gap, the day's churn
between the file's generation and the query. Closing it is what the change feed is
for, not a defect in either number.

Personal names appear in this register (roles, sole proprietorships). They are
lawfully public: Norwegian law requires the persons connected to a registered
organisation to be in the register. That is a ruling from Terje on 2026-09-11, not
an assumption made here.

dimensions.meaning: The organisation's nine-digit national identifier, and the table's primary key
dimensions.value_format: 9 digits, leading zeros significant — always text, never a number
dimensions.notes: Stable for the life of the organisation and retained after deletion from the register, which is why it is a safe join key and why the change feed can address a row that no longer has a live entity behind it. Storing it as an integer loses leading zeros; several real orgnr begin with 0.

dimensions.meaning: The upstream Enhet object exactly as Brreg published it
dimensions.value_format: jsonb object, ~30 top-level keys, several nested
dimensions.notes: Not flattened and not indexed. Contains navn, organisasjonsform, forretningsadresse, naeringskode1..3, registreringsdatoEnhetsregisteret, konkurs / underAvvikling flags and more. A GIN index over it was measured at +42% storage (~0.8 GB) for an access pattern nothing uses — see the migration header. Read fields through dbt models, not through jsonb paths in ad-hoc SQL.

dimensions.meaning: The date of the bulk file this row was loaded from
dimensions.value_format: date, or null when the download sent no Last-Modified
dimensions.notes: Provenance of the transfer, not of the organisation. The organisation's own registration and update dates live inside doc. Null is honest — a guessed date would be worse than an absent one.

dimensions.meaning: When Atlas last wrote this row
dimensions.notes: Updated by every upsert, so it tracks Atlas's load rather than any upstream event. A row whose loaded_at is older than the newest snapshot means the bootstrap did not reach it, not that the organisation is stale.

citation.text: Brønnøysundregistrene. (n.d.). Enhetsregisteret — alle registrerte enheter. Retrieved from https://data.brreg.no/enhetsregisteret/api/dokumentasjon. Available in Atlas at https://atlas.sovereignsky.no/datasets/brreg-enheter-alle.

consuming_marts.description_short: What Atlas publishes, one row per queryable endpoint: how many records it serves, when its data last arrived, and where those rows came from.
consuming_marts.description_full:
What Atlas publishes, one row per queryable endpoint: how many records it
serves, when its data last arrived, and where those rows came from.

Asked for by Røde Kors — "validate that all datasets that are ingested has
an endpoint and it can be queried … count the number of records each
endpoint has and update the last time it ingested data."

⚠️ THE GRAIN IS PER ENDPOINT, NOT PER SOURCE. meta_sources answers "what
did Atlas ingest"; this answers "what can I query, and is there anything
in it". One source can feed several endpoints and one endpoint can draw on
several sources, so the two row counts are not comparable and summing
sources will not reproduce an endpoint's count.

⚠️ atlas_inventory does not list ITSELF. It is built from the same seed it
reports on, so counting itself would be circular and the number would be
whatever the table held mid-build. 19 endpoints are listed; 20 are
published.

consuming_marts.description_short: Every organisation registered in Norway — the whole of Brønnøysundregistrene's Enhetsregisteret, around 1.17 million rows, current as of the last change-feed run.
consuming_marts.description_full:
Every organisation registered in Norway — the whole of Brønnøysundregistrene's
Enhetsregisteret, around 1.17 million rows, current as of the last change-feed run.
Companies, foundations, associations, public bodies and sole proprietorships.

🔵 CHECK WHETHER YOUR RESULT WAS TRUNCATED, AND DO NOT CHECK IT
AGAINST YOUR OWN `limit`. Send `Prefer: count=exact` and compare the
total in the `Content-Range` response header against the number of
rows you actually received:

    Content-Range: 0-4/1175169   with 5 rows  ->  truncated

Comparing `rows.length` against your own `limit=N` cannot see the cap
that matters. A server-side `db-max-rows` applies BELOW your limit, so
a cap of 1 000 against `limit=20000` returns 1 000 rows and the
comparison passes. It measures your intent, not the server's answer.
(The recipe is a consumer's, relayed on urb-agents #1410.)

🔵 Nobody can read `db-max-rows` from outside — PostgREST exposes no
endpoint for its effective settings, so "unset" and "set above N" are
indistinguishable. A cap is only ever discoverable by exceeding it.
Atlas has it UNSET today; this check keeps you correct if that changes.

🔴 THE COUNT IS WHAT COSTS, AND ONLY WHEN YOUR FILTER CANNOT USE AN
INDEX. Measured against this relation 2026-09-23:

    kommune_nr=eq.1103  + count=exact      0.10 s   27 765 rows
    navn=ilike.*...*    + count=exact     10.87 s      428 rows
    navn=ilike.*...*    without the count  0.16 s      428 rows
    no filter           + count=exact      0.50 s   1 175 169

⚠️ Adding the count to that pattern query cost 70x on a result of 428
rows. `count=exact` cannot stop at your limit — it counts every
matching row — so an unindexed predicate scans all 1.17 million.

⚠️ AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE SAID "DO NOT SEND count=exact WITH
A FILTER". That is too broad — an equality filter on `kommune_nr` came
back in 0.10 s above — and the advice would have pushed consumers off a
cheap, correct call.

🔵 MEASURE YOUR OWN PREDICATE RATHER THAN TRUSTING A LIST OF COLUMNS.
`organisasjonsnummer` carries a unique index. `kommune_nr` appears only
inside a PARTIAL index restricted to voluntary, active rows, so whether
a bare `kommune_nr` filter can use it depends on the rest of your
query. The timings above are measurements, not query plans — this
relation is not introspectable from outside, and the cheap experiment
is to send your real query twice, once with the count and once
without.

⚠️ INSIDE A BROWSER FETCH A SLOW COUNT IS A TIMEOUT, NOT A SLOW
ANSWER. A consumer diagnosed one as a CORS failure, because a request
that never completes is indistinguishable from a blocked one on the
fetch side. CORS is fine (urb-agents #1361).

🔴 AND DO NOT SUBSTITUTE `count=planned` AS THE DETECTOR. It is fast
(0.16 s on the pattern above) and its error is unbounded in BOTH
directions. Measured 2026-09-23:

    navn ilike *zzzzqqq*   planned    118   exact         0
    navn ilike *frivillig* planned    118
    navn ilike *røde*      planned    118
    navn ilike *as*        planned 570 606
    no filter              planned 1 176 875  exact 1 175 169

⚠️ 118 for a pattern that matches NOTHING, and the same 118 for three
unrelated patterns — for those it is not an estimate of your query at
all, it is the planner's fallback guess. `*as*` gets a real estimate,
so it is not a constant either; you cannot tell which you got.

🔴 And unfiltered it reports 1 706 MORE rows than exist. A detector
built on it would raise a FALSE TRUNCATION ALARM on a complete answer
— the opposite failure to the one you were guarding against, and just
as silent.

`count=estimated` does not help — measured 10.99 s, because it falls
back to an exact count when the planner's estimate is small. Use
`planned` only where an order of magnitude will do, never to decide
completeness.

Kilde: Brønnøysundregistrene. Inneholder data under norsk lisens for offentlige data
(NLOD) tilgjengeliggjort av Brønnøysundregistrene — https://data.norge.no/nlod/no/2.0.
Re-users must carry this attribution onward; it is a condition of the licence, not a
courtesy.

Deleted organisations are excluded. Brreg reports deletions through its change feed and
Atlas applies them, so an organisation removed upstream disappears from here — but the
version history is kept, so what it looked like before removal remains answerable.

Completeness caveat: this reflects deletions Brreg REPORTS. A row Atlas holds that Brreg
never had would not be removed by any automatic path, because no change event would ever
mention it.

consuming_marts.title: Voluntary organisations per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: Active voluntary organisations per kommune and ICNPO category — the number a consumer previously had to download the whole register to compute.
consuming_marts.description_full:
Active voluntary organisations per kommune and ICNPO category —
the number a consumer previously had to download the whole
register to compute. Published as api_v1.kommune_ngo_summary.

PostgREST has aggregates disabled, so `?select=count()` returns
400 and the only alternatives were ~15 minutes of per-kommune
probes or a 2.8 MB CSV on every page load. One consumer shipped
the download (urb-agents #1250, finding 1); this replaces it with
~12 000 rows.

⚠️ Counts here will NOT match a count over brreg_enhet. 7 488 of
72 792 active voluntary units (10.3 %) carry no kommune_nr — that
is what Brreg publishes — and cannot be attributed to a
municipality. A handful more sit on codes outside the 357 active
kommuner and are dropped by the join.

A (kommune, category) pair absent from this view has zero
organisations; rows are not emitted for empty combinations.

⚠️ CHANGED 2026-09-21: SSB's 9999 'Uoppgitt' is no longer
included. It is a current code, so `is_active` never excluded it,
and this relation had been reporting a place that does not exist.
Counts drop by that row. `dim_kommune` still carries 9999 — the
dimension mirrors SSB's list — and the value is published in
`unattributed_totals` (urb-agents #1301).

⚠️ COST, AND ONE LOAD-BEARING DEPENDENCY. Measured end-to-end
against the live API: 0.12 s filtered by kommune_nr, 0.205-0.326 s
unfiltered for all rows. Before the covering index on
dim_brreg_enhet it was 25 s cold for a 24 kB response and one
request timed out. That index is not an optimisation — drop it and
this relation is unusable rather than slow.

consuming_marts.title: Voluntary organisations per kommune, total
consuming_marts.description_short: One row per kommune: how many active voluntary organisations are registered there.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per kommune: how many active voluntary organisations are
registered there. 357 rows instead of the ~5 400 in
kommune_ngo_summary. Published as api_v1.kommune_ngo_totals.

Exists because PostgREST cannot sum — `?select=active_count.sum()`
returns PGRST123, aggregates are disabled — so a consumer wanting
one number per kommune otherwise fetches every category row and
adds them client-side. That was most of a cold page load
(urb-agents #1265).

⚠️ Counts exclude the 10.3 % of active voluntary units carrying no
kommune_nr, exactly as kommune_ngo_summary does. Summing this gives
the placed total, not the register total.

⚠️ CHANGED 2026-09-21: SSB's 9999 'Uoppgitt' is no longer
included. It is a current code, so `is_active` never excluded it,
and this relation had been reporting a place that does not exist.
Counts drop by that row. `dim_kommune` still carries 9999 — the
dimension mirrors SSB's list — and the value is published in
`unattributed_totals` (urb-agents #1301).

⚠️ COST, AND ONE LOAD-BEARING DEPENDENCY. Measured end-to-end
against the live API: 0.12 s filtered by kommune_nr, 0.205-0.326 s
unfiltered for all rows. Before the covering index on
dim_brreg_enhet it was 25 s cold for a 24 kB response and one
request timed out. That index is not an optimisation — drop it and
this relation is unusable rather than slow.

consuming_marts.description_short: The part of a published quantity that belongs to no municipality.
consuming_marts.description_full:
The part of a published quantity that belongs to no municipality.
Published as api_v1.unattributed_totals.

🔴 Atlas had no convention for this, and the two surfaces that met
it chose opposite wrong answers: SSB's 9999 'Uoppgitt' sits INSIDE
a per-kommune relation and corrupts any sum over it, while 7 488
active voluntary units with no kommune_nr fall OUT of one and
vanish silently. One smuggles the remainder in as a row, the other
discards it, and a consumer summing either gets a number that is
wrong in a direction it cannot see (urb-agents #700, #1250, #1265).

✅ The rule this establishes: the VALUE belongs, the ROW does not.
A per-kommune relation carries only kommuner; the remainder lives
here, named, so reconciling to a national total is a deliberate
act rather than an accident of whether a sentinel survived a
filter.

⚠️ It does NOT remove the 9999 rows from dim_kommune or
coverage_gap_barnefattigdom. That is a breaking contract change —
`?is_active=eq.true` would return 357 instead of 358 with no
warning — and it is deliberately not bundled with an additive
change. `is_sentinel` remains a stopgap and this view does not
make the trap gone.

🔵 A zero is a result. Where the remainder is genuinely nothing
this emits 0 rather than omitting the row: "we checked, none" and
"nobody checked" are different answers, and a missing row cannot
tell them apart.

✅ THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES, AND A TEST SAYS SO. Summing a per-kommune
relation and adding every `unattributed_value` for it must equal
`total_value`:

    kommune_ngo_totals   65 270
    no_kommune_nr         7 489
    kommune_nr_not_current   43
    ---------------------------
    total_value          72 802

⚠️ It did not close on the day this shipped. It named 7 489 of
7 532 and the 43 Svalbard organisations were counted by neither
relation — silent, self-consistent, and visible only by doing the
subtraction this view exists to support. The singular test
`the_remainder_closes_the_total` now asserts the decomposition
rather than the parts, which is the thing that was missing: every
part had a test and the relationship between them had none.

sources.description:
Brønnøysundregistrene's Frivillighetsregisteret holds the ~72,800 Norwegian
organisations registered as voluntary. Atlas walks it in full and stores each
record verbatim in `raw.brreg_frivillige`, typing out the registrant's own ICNPO
classification.

🔴 This is not where Atlas learns which organisations are voluntary. That flag —
`registrertIFrivillighetsregisteret` — is on 100% of Enhetsregisteret's bulk
records and true for ~72,798 of them, so the NGO population is derived from the
snapshot alone with no second API call. This source exists for the attributes
Enhetsregisteret does not carry: `icnpoKategorier`, `grasrotandel`,
`innfoertDato`, `vedtekter` and `regnskapsrapportering`.

That split was designed in deliberately. If this register becomes unavailable,
the membership half of Atlas's NGO population survives untouched and only the
enrichment half needs rethinking.
sources.attribution: Inneholder data under norsk lisens for offentlige data (NLOD) tilgjengeliggjort av Brønnøysundregistrene
sources.methodology_notes:
🔴 This API is the exact opposite of the Enhetsregister change feed, and the
opposite mistake is available in each. Measured 2026-09-12:

|  | oppdateringer/enheter | frivillige-organisasjoner |
|---|---|---|
| `page=` | works, capped at 20 — the trap | rejected, HTTP 400 even at page=0 |
| `_links.next` | built with `page=` — the trap | `searchAfter=`, the only way to walk |
| `size` max | ≥ 10,000 | 100 (101 → 400) |
| `page` block | present, totalElements usable | absent — no backlog signal at all |

So the change feed must never follow `_links.next` and this source must do
nothing else. A house rule of either "always follow next" or "never follow next"
would be wrong for exactly one of them.

There is no change feed and no bulk download for this register: `/oppdateringer`,
`/oppdateringer/frivillige-organisasjoner` and `/frivillige-organisasjoner/lastned`
all return 404. A full re-walk is the only option — ~727 requests at the size cap
of 100, a few minutes. The load upserts, so a walk that finds nothing new is a
no-op.

⚠️ The endpoint was reported as 404 by another agent on urb-agents #711. It is
not: the report tested `/frivillighetsregisteret/api`, its `/dokumentasjon`, and
the camelCase `/frivilligeOrganisasjoner`, none of which is the hyphenated path
above. Three consecutive requests here returned 200.

dimensions.meaning: The organisation's nine-digit identifier, and the join key to Enhetsregisteret
dimensions.value_format: 9 digits, leading zeros significant — always text
dimensions.notes: Also the pagination key: this API walks by `searchAfter=<last organisasjonsnummer>` rather than by page number.

dimensions.meaning: Primary ICNPO code as the organisation classified itself
dimensions.notes: 🟢 Taken from `icnpoKategorier` at `rekkefoelge` 1, not array position 0 — the array is not guaranteed sorted and taking the first element would silently promote a secondary classification. The registrant's own classification is better evidence than one derived from a NACE industry code, which is the route available for organisations NOT in this register.
Paired with icnpo_nummer from the same array element. Null when the organisation declares none.

dimensions.meaning: The upstream record exactly as Brreg published it
dimensions.notes: Holds frivilligOrganisasjonsstatus, kontonummer, innfoertDato, foersteGangInnfoert, grasrotandel, regnskapsrapportering, vedtekter, paategninger and the complete icnpoKategorier array including any secondary categories the typed columns do not carry.

citation.text: Brønnøysundregistrene. (n.d.). Frivillighetsregisteret — frivillige organisasjoner. Retrieved from https://www.brreg.no/om-oss/registrene-vare/om-frivillighetsregisteret/. Available in Atlas at https://atlas.sovereignsky.no/datasets/brreg-frivillige.

sources.description:
Brønnøysundregistrene publishes every change to Enhetsregisteret as an ordered
feed: one record per change, carrying the organisation number, a change type and
a monotonic `oppdateringsid`. Atlas walks it forward daily from a durable
watermark, recording each change in `raw.brreg_oppdateringer` and the
organisation's document at that moment in `raw.brreg_enheter_versions`.

This is what keeps the bulk snapshot (`brreg-enheter-alle`) from going stale.
The snapshot is a point in time; a bulk file cannot express a deletion, because
absence from a 1.17M-record file is indistinguishable from a truncated download.
Deletions arrive here, as `Sletting` and `Fjernet` change types.

The feed has no retention window — it reaches back to `oppdateringsid` 1 in April
2018 — so a missed day, week or month catches up completely on the next run.
Cadence is a freshness choice, not a correctness one.
sources.attribution: Inneholder data under norsk lisens for offentlige data (NLOD) tilgjengeliggjort av Brønnøysundregistrene
sources.methodology_notes:
🔴 The feed is walked by CURSOR ONLY — `?oppdateringsid=<last+1>&size=10000`.

`page` is capped at 20, and Brreg's HAL `_links.next` is built with `page=`, so
following the next link — the idiomatic, careful thing to do — returns HTTP 400
after 20 hops having seen only the oldest 10,000 changes, every one of them
`Ukjent`, and not a single deletion. It would look perfectly healthy. A
source-text test asserts the module contains neither `page=` nor `_links.next`.

Termination is an ABSENT `_embedded` key, not an empty array: a caught-up
response is `{_links, page}` with `totalElements: 0`. A poller spelled
`body._embedded.oppdaterteEnheter` throws at exactly the moment it catches up.

The watermark lives in `raw.brreg_feed_watermark`, not in a Dagster cursor. A
cursor lives in the Dagster instance database, which has a different lifecycle;
if it is rebuilt, a cursor-based feed restarts from nowhere and silently stops
applying deletions.

A run is capped at 50,000 changes (`BRREG_FEED_MAX_CHANGES`). Each change costs
one entity fetch, and a watermark of 1 would mean 16.4M requests against a
public-sector API Atlas depends on staying welcome at.

dimensions.meaning: Brreg's monotonic change identifier, and the cursor the feed is walked by
dimensions.notes: 🔴 Sparse, and that matters. The id space runs to ~25.18M against ~16.4M records, so the gap between two ids is NOT the number of changes between them — asking for id 16,417,000 returns a first record of 16,427,801. Never compute a backlog by subtracting ids; read `page.totalElements` at the cursor, which is a correct remaining-record count.

dimensions.meaning: What kind of change Brreg recorded
dimensions.value_format: Ny, Endring, Sletting, Fjernet or Ukjent
dimensions.notes: All five occur and all five are handled. `Sletting` is the deletion in current traffic; `Fjernet` is real but concentrated in older eras (23 of 500 at oppdateringsid 16,400,000, and absent from the 2026-09-11 daily sample); `Ukjent` is the entire pre-2018-08 history and must never delete anything. Stored verbatim and not constrained to an enum — a sixth value must land and be counted, not rejected at the door.

dimensions.meaning: The organisation the change is about
dimensions.value_format: 9 digits, leading zeros significant — always text
dimensions.notes: Joins to raw.brreg_enheter_snapshot. Retained after deletion, which is what lets a tombstone address a row that no longer has a live entity behind it.

dimensions.meaning: The organisation's document as it stood when the change was received
dimensions.value_format: jsonb, or null when the entity fetch failed
dimensions.notes: ⚠️ For a `Sletting` this is Brreg's SIX-KEY STUB, not a full record — a deleted organisation still answers HTTP 200 with `slettedato` set. Branch on endringstype; never assume doc is a complete Enhet, and never detect deletion from a status code.

dimensions.meaning: What Atlas did with the change
dimensions.notes: Derived from endringstype at load time. `skipped_unknown` covers both `Ukjent` and any future sixth value, deliberately — the run counts and surfaces them rather than guessing an action.

citation.text: Brønnøysundregistrene. (n.d.). Enhetsregisteret — oppdateringer (endringsfeed). Retrieved from https://data.brreg.no/enhetsregisteret/api/dokumentasjon. Available in Atlas at https://atlas.sovereignsky.no/datasets/brreg-oppdateringer.

consuming_marts.description_full:
What Atlas publishes, one row per queryable endpoint: how many records it
serves, when its data last arrived, and where those rows came from.

Asked for by Røde Kors — "validate that all datasets that are ingested has
an endpoint and it can be queried … count the number of records each
endpoint has and update the last time it ingested data."

⚠️ THE GRAIN IS PER ENDPOINT, NOT PER SOURCE. meta_sources answers "what
did Atlas ingest"; this answers "what can I query, and is there anything
in it". One source can feed several endpoints and one endpoint can draw on
several sources, so the two row counts are not comparable and summing
sources will not reproduce an endpoint's count.

reports on, so counting itself would be circular and the number would be

consuming_marts.description_short: Every organisation registered in Norway — the whole of Brønnøysundregistrene's Enhetsregisteret, around 1.17 million rows, current as of the last change-feed run.
consuming_marts.description_full:
Every organisation registered in Norway — the whole of Brønnøysundregistrene's
Enhetsregisteret, around 1.17 million rows, current as of the last change-feed run.
Companies, foundations, associations, public bodies and sole proprietorships.

🔵 CHECK WHETHER YOUR RESULT WAS TRUNCATED, AND DO NOT CHECK IT
AGAINST YOUR OWN `limit`. Send `Prefer: count=exact` and compare the
total in the `Content-Range` response header against the number of
rows you actually received:

    Content-Range: 0-4/1175169   with 5 rows  ->  truncated

Comparing `rows.length` against your own `limit=N` cannot see the cap
that matters. A server-side `db-max-rows` applies BELOW your limit, so
a cap of 1 000 against `limit=20000` returns 1 000 rows and the
comparison passes. It measures your intent, not the server's answer.
(The recipe is a consumer's, relayed on urb-agents #1410.)

🔵 Nobody can read `db-max-rows` from outside — PostgREST exposes no
endpoint for its effective settings, so "unset" and "set above N" are
indistinguishable. A cap is only ever discoverable by exceeding it.
Atlas has it UNSET today; this check keeps you correct if that changes.

🔴 THE COUNT IS WHAT COSTS, AND ONLY WHEN YOUR FILTER CANNOT USE AN
INDEX. Measured against this relation 2026-09-23:

    kommune_nr=eq.1103  + count=exact      0.10 s   27 765 rows
    navn=ilike.*...*    + count=exact     10.87 s      428 rows
    navn=ilike.*...*    without the count  0.16 s      428 rows
    no filter           + count=exact      0.50 s   1 175 169

⚠️ Adding the count to that pattern query cost 70x on a result of 428
rows. `count=exact` cannot stop at your limit — it counts every
matching row — so an unindexed predicate scans all 1.17 million.

⚠️ AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE SAID "DO NOT SEND count=exact WITH
A FILTER". That is too broad — an equality filter on `kommune_nr` came
back in 0.10 s above — and the advice would have pushed consumers off a
cheap, correct call.

🔵 MEASURE YOUR OWN PREDICATE RATHER THAN TRUSTING A LIST OF COLUMNS.
`organisasjonsnummer` carries a unique index. `kommune_nr` appears only
inside a PARTIAL index restricted to voluntary, active rows, so whether
a bare `kommune_nr` filter can use it depends on the rest of your
query. The timings above are measurements, not query plans — this
relation is not introspectable from outside, and the cheap experiment
is to send your real query twice, once with the count and once
without.

⚠️ INSIDE A BROWSER FETCH A SLOW COUNT IS A TIMEOUT, NOT A SLOW
ANSWER. A consumer diagnosed one as a CORS failure, because a request
that never completes is indistinguishable from a blocked one on the
fetch side. CORS is fine (urb-agents #1361).

🔴 AND DO NOT SUBSTITUTE `count=planned` AS THE DETECTOR. It is fast
(0.16 s on the pattern above) and its error is unbounded in BOTH
directions. Measured 2026-09-23:

    navn ilike *zzzzqqq*   planned    118   exact         0
    navn ilike *frivillig* planned    118
    navn ilike *røde*      planned    118
    navn ilike *as*        planned 570 606
    no filter              planned 1 176 875  exact 1 175 169

⚠️ 118 for a pattern that matches NOTHING, and the same 118 for three
unrelated patterns — for those it is not an estimate of your query at
all, it is the planner's fallback guess. `*as*` gets a real estimate,
so it is not a constant either; you cannot tell which you got.

🔴 And unfiltered it reports 1 706 MORE rows than exist. A detector
built on it would raise a FALSE TRUNCATION ALARM on a complete answer
— the opposite failure to the one you were guarding against, and just
as silent.

`count=estimated` does not help — measured 10.99 s, because it falls
back to an exact count when the planner's estimate is small. Use
`planned` only where an order of magnitude will do, never to decide
completeness.

Re-users must carry this attribution onward; it is a condition of the licence, not a
courtesy.

Deleted organisations are excluded. Brreg reports deletions through its change feed and
Atlas applies them, so an organisation removed upstream disappears from here — but the
version history is kept, so what it looked like before removal remains answerable.

Completeness caveat: this reflects deletions Brreg REPORTS. A row Atlas holds that Brreg

sources.description:
Barne-, ungdoms- og familiedirektoratet (Bufdir) publishes the Barnefattigdom kommunemonitor on
bufdir.no and ships a single bulk ZIP of `Indikator_*.xlsx` workbooks ("last ned hele datasettet").
Atlas downloads that ZIP (URL discovered from the monitor page), parses sheet `Data` in each
workbook, and loads kommune- and sub-kommune-level time series into `raw.bufdir_barnefattigdom`
so analysts can compare Bufdir's poverty lens with register-based sources such as SSB low-income
statistics.
sources.attribution: Kilde: Barne-, ungdoms- og familiedirektoratet, Barnefattigdom kommunemonitor
sources.methodology_notes: Children under 18 living in households below 60% of the national median equivalised income (EU-scale). Spines differ per indicator — some series start in 2013, others in 2015 or later. Bufdir's poverty lens complements SSB's register-based measures by adding bydel-level breakdowns for the largest kommuner.

dimensions.meaning: Stable surrogate indicator key for ZIP workbook rows (not Strapi)
dimensions.notes: Derived as SHA-256 fingerprint of the `Indikator_*.xlsx` filename stem; breaks if Bufdir renames workbook files inside the ZIP.

dimensions.meaning: Geographic code from workbook column Region
dimensions.value_format: 0 (land), 2-digit fylke, 4-digit kommune, or longer codes for bydel/delbydel
dimensions.notes: Rows follow whatever geography levels each indicator publishes.

dimensions.meaning: Workbook column Enhet (first category axis), normalised lowercase
dimensions.notes: Mirrors the paired rows in each Data sheet for child vs household units.

dimensions.meaning: Workbook column Tallformat (second category axis), normalised lowercase
dimensions.notes: Paired with category_unit — four tuples per workbook × geography when all rows exist upstream.

dimensions.meaning: Calendar year column from workbook header row
dimensions.notes: Spines differ by indicator — see values_json for the full year map before filtering NAs.

dimensions.meaning: Parsed year→value map for the geography and Enhet/Tallformat tuple
dimensions.value_format: JSON object with string year keys; suppressed cells as null
dimensions.notes: Matches prior raw semantics (full spine per slice); mart reads scalar `value` for the keyed year row.

consuming_marts.title: Latest indicator values per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each
indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner. Backs the
data explorer's per-indicator detail page (atlas-frontend
/data/[source_id]/[contents_code]) and is the equivalent of the
loadIndicatorValues() inline query.

🔴 ROW COUNT IS NOT COVERAGE. A row exists for every active kommune
the source publishes at all, INCLUDING those where `value` is null.
So a series returns ~357 rows whether 357 kommuner have a number or
66 do, and counting rows overstates coverage by up to five times.

⚠️ This has always been true and became dangerous on 2026-09-21,
when nine Ungdata sources published at 18-43 % kommune coverage
against SSB register sources at nearly 100 %. `fhi-hasj` returns
357 rows carrying 66 values.

✅ `indicator_summary.kommuner_with_value` is the live count and the
only thing to trust. It is not restated here on purpose — a number
copied into a description goes stale, which is the defect that made
`fhi-depresjon` advertise fourteen years of data it never held.

PostgREST consumers filter via
?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. The full table is the
cross-product of every indicator with every active kommune that
has a row at latest_year, so the unfiltered row count is large
(~360 active kommuner × ~70 indicators in v1).

Inactive kommuner (kommune_is_active = false) are excluded so the
output reflects today's kommune set, not historical codes that
upstream still emits.

consuming_marts.title: Indicator coverage gaps per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: 🔴 A ROW HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LOW NEED.
consuming_marts.description_full:
🔴 A ROW HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LOW NEED. For `fhi-*` sources it is
usually FHI's disclosure suppression: it hides numbers based on fewer
than ~6 cases, and hides a whole series when more than 20% of it is
hidden, "for ikke å skape et skjevt inntrykk av situasjonen i
kommunen" — to avoid a skewed impression of that kommune.

⚠️ Measured: 105 kommuner are missing from 10+ `fhi-*` series, median
population 1,452, monotonic in population, and EVERY kommune is absent
from at least three. Treating absence as zero in a ranked index
inverts the signal for the smallest kommuner (urb-agents #1379). See
`indicator_summary.kommuners_with_null`.

One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) for every
active kommune that has *no* non-NULL value at the indicator's
latest_year. The "coverage gap" sidebar on the data explorer
detail page; equivalent to the listMissingKommuner() inline query.

?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. Membership semantics: a
kommune is considered "missing" if it either has no row at
latest_year, or has a row with value IS NULL. Status markers (':',

unfiltered row count is the per-indicator gap-list aggregated

consuming_marts.description_full: Per-source indicator relation for `fhi-alkohol` (Folkehelseinstituttet), published at the grain the publisher actually uses rather than flattened into the cross-source views. 🔴 stability:source — the column set here follows Folkehelseinstituttet, not Atlas. consuming_marts.description_short: One row per queryable Atlas endpoint, with tags inherited from upstream sources via the lineage graph and a `layer:<schema>` tag from the schema.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per queryable Atlas endpoint, with tags inherited from
upstream sources via the lineage graph and a `layer:<schema>` tag
from the schema. Wraps to `api_v1.meta_endpoints` and backs the
tag-filter catalogue at `/data` in the customer frontend
(PLAN-007 phase 4).

🔵 THIS IS THE INDEX, SO IT SAYS WHERE THE OTHER TWO CATALOGUES
ARE: `meta_sources` for one row per ingest source (licence,
publisher, freshness), and `meta_dimensions` for one row per
source × upstream dimension — what each coded column means and
its value format. A consumer enumerating relations here should
not have to read 19 descriptions to discover the second one
(urb-agents #1335).

Includes endpoints from `api_v1.*`, `marts.*`, and `raw.*`
(Atlas's three open-by-default schemas; `private_marts.*` stays
auth-gated and is excluded). Skips internal seeds prefixed `_`
(`_sources_manifest`, `_sources_dimensions`) and any `dbt_*`
diagnostic tables.

Tag inheritance uses the **union** rule: a `mart_*` derived from
many sources picks up every source's `provider:`, `topic:`,
`geo:`, `cadence:`, and `eu_theme:` tag, deduped. Filter
"involves something annual" beats "purely annual" — see PLAN-007
phase 3.2 for the design rationale.

consuming_marts.description_short: Per-source catalogue row — one per ingest source in `_sources_manifest`, joined to `raw.ingest_runs` aggregates so consumers see freshness alongside the static metadata.
consuming_marts.description_full:
Per-source catalogue row — one per ingest source in
`_sources_manifest`, joined to `raw.ingest_runs` aggregates so
consumers see freshness alongside the static metadata. Wraps to
`api_v1.meta_sources` and backs `/data/sources` in the customer
frontend (PLAN-007 phase 4).

🔴 THIS RELATION DESCRIBES A SOURCE, NOT ITS COLUMNS. For what an
upstream dimension MEANS — what `AAR` is, whether a code is a
kommune, whether a year is a single year or a window — read
`meta_dimensions`, one row per source × dimension with the
upstream's own words and the value format.

⚠️ THIS POINTER EXISTS BECAUSE ITS ABSENCE COST A DAY. On
2026-09-21 a consumer read all 21 descriptions here, concluded
"exactly two sources use multi-year windows", and shipped a wrong
year on a front page. `meta_dimensions` said `"3-year rolling
cohort"` for a third the whole time. Reading every row of this
relation is thorough and structurally incapable of answering a
question about a dimension (urb-agents #1335).

Tags column is a Postgres `text[]` carrying the four declared
namespaces (`provider:`, `topic:`, `geo:`, `cadence:`) plus the
`eu_theme:` namespace. The customer frontend renders each as a
filter pill; PostgREST consumers filter via `?tags=cs.{"provider:ssb"}`
— the quotes are required, because the value contains a colon.

`last_ingested_at` and `last_upstream_update_at` come from
`raw.ingest_runs` aggregated over successful (`exit_code = 0`)
runs. Sources whose ingest module hasn't yet captured the
upstream's "updated" field leave `last_upstream_update_at` NULL —
that's the design (`raw.ingest_runs.upstream_updated_at` is
nullable per migration 028).

`downstream_model_count` is the number of distinct dbt models
that derive from this source via the `lineage` seed (Phase 3.3).
0 for sources whose data hasn't yet been wired into a mart.

consuming_marts.description_short: The part of a published quantity that belongs to no municipality.
consuming_marts.description_full:
The part of a published quantity that belongs to no municipality.
Published as api_v1.unattributed_totals.

🔴 Atlas had no convention for this, and the two surfaces that met
it chose opposite wrong answers: SSB's 9999 'Uoppgitt' sits INSIDE
a per-kommune relation and corrupts any sum over it, while 7 488
active voluntary units with no kommune_nr fall OUT of one and
vanish silently. One smuggles the remainder in as a row, the other
discards it, and a consumer summing either gets a number that is
wrong in a direction it cannot see (urb-agents #700, #1250, #1265).

✅ The rule this establishes: the VALUE belongs, the ROW does not.
A per-kommune relation carries only kommuner; the remainder lives
here, named, so reconciling to a national total is a deliberate
act rather than an accident of whether a sentinel survived a
filter.

⚠️ It does NOT remove the 9999 rows from dim_kommune or
coverage_gap_barnefattigdom. That is a breaking contract change —
`?is_active=eq.true` would return 357 instead of 358 with no
warning — and it is deliberately not bundled with an additive
change. `is_sentinel` remains a stopgap and this view does not
make the trap gone.

🔵 A zero is a result. Where the remainder is genuinely nothing
this emits 0 rather than omitting the row: "we checked, none" and
"nobody checked" are different answers, and a missing row cannot
tell them apart.

✅ THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES, AND A TEST SAYS SO. Summing a per-kommune
relation and adding every `unattributed_value` for it must equal
`total_value`:

    kommune_ngo_totals   65 270
    no_kommune_nr         7 489
    kommune_nr_not_current   43
    ---------------------------
    total_value          72 802

⚠️ It did not close on the day this shipped. It named 7 489 of
7 532 and the 43 Svalbard organisations were counted by neither
relation — silent, self-consistent, and visible only by doing the
subtraction this view exists to support. The singular test
`the_remainder_closes_the_total` now asserts the decomposition
rather than the parts, which is the thing that was missing: every
part had a test and the relationship between them had none.

sources.description: FHI Folkehelsestatistikk table 338 — Befolkningssammensetning. Population counts by region × sex × age band, used as the demographic denominator across other indicators (per-capita rates, age structure).

dimensions.notes: ~409 codes — 0 (national), 2-digit fylke, 4-digit kommune, 6-digit bydel

TELLER (count) only — RATE / SMR are derivable downstream from these counts.

consuming_marts.title: Latest indicator values per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each
indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner. Backs the

only thing to trust. It is not restated here on purpose — a number
copied into a description goes stale, which is the defect that made
`fhi-depresjon` advertise fourteen years of data it never held.

cross-product of every indicator with every active kommune that

consuming_marts.description_short: One row per queryable Atlas endpoint, with tags inherited from upstream sources via the lineage graph and a `layer:<schema>` tag from the schema.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per queryable Atlas endpoint, with tags inherited from
upstream sources via the lineage graph and a `layer:<schema>` tag
from the schema. Wraps to `api_v1.meta_endpoints` and backs the

`_sources_manifest`, joined to `raw.ingest_runs` aggregates so
consumers see freshness alongside the static metadata. Wraps to
`api_v1.meta_sources` and backs `/data/sources` in the customer
frontend (PLAN-007 phase 4).

🔴 THIS RELATION DESCRIBES A SOURCE, NOT ITS COLUMNS. For what an
upstream dimension MEANS — what `AAR` is, whether a code is a
kommune, whether a year is a single year or a window — read
`meta_dimensions`, one row per source × dimension with the
upstream's own words and the value format.

⚠️ THIS POINTER EXISTS BECAUSE ITS ABSENCE COST A DAY. On
2026-09-21 a consumer read all 21 descriptions here, concluded
"exactly two sources use multi-year windows", and shipped a wrong
year on a front page. `meta_dimensions` said `"3-year rolling
cohort"` for a third the whole time. Reading every row of this
relation is thorough and structurally incapable of answering a
question about a dimension (urb-agents #1335).

Tags column is a Postgres `text[]` carrying the four declared
namespaces (`provider:`, `topic:`, `geo:`, `cadence:`) plus the
`eu_theme:` namespace. The customer frontend renders each as a
filter pill; PostgREST consumers filter via `?tags=cs.{"provider:ssb"}`
— the quotes are required, because the value contains a colon.

`last_ingested_at` and `last_upstream_update_at` come from
`raw.ingest_runs` aggregated over successful (`exit_code = 0`)
runs. Sources whose ingest module hasn't yet captured the
upstream's "updated" field leave `last_upstream_update_at` NULL —
that's the design (`raw.ingest_runs.upstream_updated_at` is
nullable per migration 028).

`downstream_model_count` is the number of distinct dbt models
that derive from this source via the `lineage` seed (Phase 3.3).
0 for sources whose data hasn't yet been wired into a mart.

consuming_marts.description_short: The part of a published quantity that belongs to no municipality.
consuming_marts.description_full:
The part of a published quantity that belongs to no municipality.
Published as api_v1.unattributed_totals.

🔴 Atlas had no convention for this, and the two surfaces that met
it chose opposite wrong answers: SSB's 9999 'Uoppgitt' sits INSIDE
a per-kommune relation and corrupts any sum over it, while 7 488
active voluntary units with no kommune_nr fall OUT of one and
vanish silently. One smuggles the remainder in as a row, the other
discards it, and a consumer summing either gets a number that is
wrong in a direction it cannot see (urb-agents #700, #1250, #1265).

✅ The rule this establishes: the VALUE belongs, the ROW does not.
A per-kommune relation carries only kommuner; the remainder lives
here, named, so reconciling to a national total is a deliberate
act rather than an accident of whether a sentinel survived a
filter.

⚠️ It does NOT remove the 9999 rows from dim_kommune or
coverage_gap_barnefattigdom. That is a breaking contract change —
`?is_active=eq.true` would return 357 instead of 358 with no
warning — and it is deliberately not bundled with an additive
change. `is_sentinel` remains a stopgap and this view does not
make the trap gone.

🔵 A zero is a result. Where the remainder is genuinely nothing
this emits 0 rather than omitting the row: "we checked, none" and
"nobody checked" are different answers, and a missing row cannot
tell them apart.

✅ THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES, AND A TEST SAYS SO. Summing a per-kommune
relation and adding every `unattributed_value` for it must equal
`total_value`:

    kommune_ngo_totals   65 270
    no_kommune_nr         7 489
    kommune_nr_not_current   43
    ---------------------------
    total_value          72 802

⚠️ It did not close on the day this shipped. It named 7 489 of
7 532 and the 43 Svalbard organisations were counted by neither
relation — silent, self-consistent, and visible only by doing the
subtraction this view exists to support. The singular test
`the_remainder_closes_the_total` now asserts the decomposition
rather than the parts, which is the thing that was missing: every
part had a test and the relationship between them had none.

sources.description: FHI Folkehelsestatistikk table 932 (INNVAND_INNVKAT) — population by immigrant category (1st-gen / 2nd-gen / combined) per region × age band. Complements fhi-innvandrere (table 175) which has country-origin granularity but no INNVKAT split. Published as table 650 until September 2026, when FHI renumbered it; the series is continuous across that change.

dimensions.notes: ~409 codes
23 single-year periods, 2003–2025
10 bands. Includes 0_120 (everyone) plus disjoint slices 0_29, 30_44, 45_64, 65_79, 80_120, etc.
"2" innvandrere (1st-gen), "3" norskfødte med innvandrerforeldre (2nd-gen), "23" combined (sum of 2 + 3 — exclude from disjoint-category sums)
Always "0" for this table — origin region is collapsed. Use fhi-innvandrere (table 175) for origin-region resolution.
TELLER (count), RATE (percent), SMR (standardised ratio vs national)

citation.text: Folkehelseinstituttet. (2025). INNVAND_INNVKAT. Retrieved from https://statistikk.fhi.no/nokkel/iTcQHmSn_g9PSQ0MRVD-gzOvgVzNXuZ_xJRCUnQ2Z1w?GEO=0&AAR=2020_2020,2021_2021,2022_2022,2023_2023,2024_2024,2025_2025&ALDER=0_120,0_29&INNVKAT=23,2,3&LANDBAK=0&MEASURE_TYPE=TELLER. Available in Atlas at https://atlas.sovereignsky.no/datasets/fhi-innvkat.

consuming_marts.description_short: What Atlas publishes, one row per queryable endpoint: how many records it serves, when its data last arrived, and where those rows came from.
consuming_marts.description_full:
What Atlas publishes, one row per queryable endpoint: how many records it
serves, when its data last arrived, and where those rows came from.

Asked for by Røde Kors — "validate that all datasets that are ingested has
an endpoint and it can be queried … count the number of records each
endpoint has and update the last time it ingested data."

⚠️ THE GRAIN IS PER ENDPOINT, NOT PER SOURCE. meta_sources answers "what
did Atlas ingest"; this answers "what can I query, and is there anything
in it". One source can feed several endpoints and one endpoint can draw on
several sources, so the two row counts are not comparable and summing
sources will not reproduce an endpoint's count.

⚠️ atlas_inventory does not list ITSELF. It is built from the same seed it
reports on, so counting itself would be circular and the number would be
whatever the table held mid-build. 19 endpoints are listed; 20 are
published.

consuming_marts.title: Child-poverty coverage gap (kommune)
consuming_marts.description_short: One row per active kommune for the latest year of SSB 08764 child poverty data, combining the EUskala60 share (% of children in low-income households) with the Personer count (number of children).
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per active kommune for the latest year of SSB 08764 child
poverty data, combining the EUskala60 share (% of children in
low-income households) with the Personer count (number of
children). Backs the barnefattigdom map page (atlas-frontend
/coverage-gap/barnefattigdom).

First member of the mart_coverage_gap_<topic> family. Future
coverage-gap maps follow the same shape: latest year per kommune,
one row per kommune, value(s) pivoted out of contents_code into
named columns. PostgREST projects this view as a single endpoint;
consumers don't filter, they read the whole map dataset in one
request.

Inactive kommuner are excluded so the map renders today's
kommune set. NULL values are kept in place — Map.tsx renders
them as "no data".

consuming_marts.title: Latest indicator values per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each
indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner. Backs the
data explorer's per-indicator detail page (atlas-frontend
/data/[source_id]/[contents_code]) and is the equivalent of the
loadIndicatorValues() inline query.

🔴 ROW COUNT IS NOT COVERAGE. A row exists for every active kommune
the source publishes at all, INCLUDING those where `value` is null.
So a series returns ~357 rows whether 357 kommuner have a number or
66 do, and counting rows overstates coverage by up to five times.

⚠️ This has always been true and became dangerous on 2026-09-21,
when nine Ungdata sources published at 18-43 % kommune coverage
against SSB register sources at nearly 100 %. `fhi-hasj` returns
357 rows carrying 66 values.

✅ `indicator_summary.kommuner_with_value` is the live count and the
only thing to trust. It is not restated here on purpose — a number
copied into a description goes stale, which is the defect that made
`fhi-depresjon` advertise fourteen years of data it never held.

PostgREST consumers filter via
?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. The full table is the
cross-product of every indicator with every active kommune that
has a row at latest_year, so the unfiltered row count is large
(~360 active kommuner × ~70 indicators in v1).

Inactive kommuner (kommune_is_active = false) are excluded so the
output reflects today's kommune set, not historical codes that
upstream still emits.

consuming_marts.title: Indicator coverage gaps per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: 🔴 A ROW HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LOW NEED.
consuming_marts.description_full:
🔴 A ROW HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LOW NEED. For `fhi-*` sources it is
usually FHI's disclosure suppression: it hides numbers based on fewer
than ~6 cases, and hides a whole series when more than 20% of it is
hidden, "for ikke å skape et skjevt inntrykk av situasjonen i
kommunen" — to avoid a skewed impression of that kommune.

⚠️ Measured: 105 kommuner are missing from 10+ `fhi-*` series, median
population 1,452, monotonic in population, and EVERY kommune is absent
from at least three. Treating absence as zero in a ranked index
inverts the signal for the smallest kommuner (urb-agents #1379). See
`indicator_summary.kommuners_with_null`.

One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) for every
active kommune that has *no* non-NULL value at the indicator's
latest_year. The "coverage gap" sidebar on the data explorer
detail page; equivalent to the listMissingKommuner() inline query.

PostgREST consumers filter via
?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. Membership semantics: a
kommune is considered "missing" if it either has no row at
latest_year, or has a row with value IS NULL. Status markers (':',
'X') do not count as a value.

The full table is the cross-product of every indicator with every
active kommune that lacks data. Most cells are present, so the
unfiltered row count is the per-indicator gap-list aggregated
across all indicators.

consuming_marts.title: Indicator coverage summary
consuming_marts.description_short: One row per (source_id, contents_code) summarising the latest-year coverage and value range for every indicator in fact_kommune_indicators.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per (source_id, contents_code) summarising the latest-year
coverage and value range for every indicator in
fact_kommune_indicators. This is the backing dataset for the data
explorer index page (atlas-frontend /data) and is the equivalent of
the listIndicators() inline query that PostgREST projects as
/mart_indicator_summary on the public API.

Query shape: latest-year-per-indicator + group-by + value/null counts
filtered to active kommuner only. Inactive kommuner (historical
codes retained by upstream) are excluded from the counts so consumers
see "how many of today's kommuner have data?" not "how many rows
exist?".

Refreshed nightly together with fact_kommune_indicators. The
upstream_updated column carries the most recent raw load timestamp
across the rows that contributed to this summary, so freshness can
be inspected per indicator without joining to raw.* sources.

consuming_marts.title: INNVAND_INNVKAT
consuming_marts.description_short: Per-source indicator relation for `fhi-innvkat` (Folkehelseinstituttet), published at the grain the publisher actually uses rather than flattened into the cross-source views.
consuming_marts.description_full: Per-source indicator relation for `fhi-innvkat` (Folkehelseinstituttet), published at the grain the publisher actually uses rather than flattened into the cross-source views. 🔴 stability:source — the column set here follows Folkehelseinstituttet, not Atlas. If the publisher adds, renames or drops a dimension, this relation changes with it. That is the deliberate trade for getting the real grain; prefer a stability:curated relation if you need a shape Atlas promises to hold still. Decode codes through meta_dimensions filtered to source_id=fhi-innvkat.

consuming_marts.description_short: One row per queryable Atlas endpoint, with tags inherited from upstream sources via the lineage graph and a `layer:<schema>` tag from the schema.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per queryable Atlas endpoint, with tags inherited from
upstream sources via the lineage graph and a `layer:<schema>` tag
from the schema. Wraps to `api_v1.meta_endpoints` and backs the
tag-filter catalogue at `/data` in the customer frontend
(PLAN-007 phase 4).

🔵 THIS IS THE INDEX, SO IT SAYS WHERE THE OTHER TWO CATALOGUES
ARE: `meta_sources` for one row per ingest source (licence,
publisher, freshness), and `meta_dimensions` for one row per
source × upstream dimension — what each coded column means and
its value format. A consumer enumerating relations here should
not have to read 19 descriptions to discover the second one
(urb-agents #1335).

Includes endpoints from `api_v1.*`, `marts.*`, and `raw.*`
(Atlas's three open-by-default schemas; `private_marts.*` stays
auth-gated and is excluded). Skips internal seeds prefixed `_`
(`_sources_manifest`, `_sources_dimensions`) and any `dbt_*`
diagnostic tables.

Tag inheritance uses the **union** rule: a `mart_*` derived from
many sources picks up every source's `provider:`, `topic:`,
`geo:`, `cadence:`, and `eu_theme:` tag, deduped. Filter
"involves something annual" beats "purely annual" — see PLAN-007
phase 3.2 for the design rationale.

sources.description: FHI Folkehelsestatistikk table 370 — KPR 1-year. Annual primary-care contact rates from the Kommunalt pasient- og brukerregister, by ICPC-2 code group × region × sex × age. Atlas's first healthcare-utilisation source; complements self-reported survey data from Ungdata.

dimensions.meaning: Region (national / fylke / kommune — no bydel resolution)
dimensions.notes: ~373 codes — narrower than other FHI tables which include bydeler

dimensions.value_format: "YYYY_YYYY" range string (single-year despite the range form)
dimensions.notes: 8 single-year periods upstream (2017–2024); Atlas pulls latest 1
"0" combined (only value Atlas ingests). Sex-stratified analysis would need a sibling source.
10 bands incl. 0_74 aggregate, 15_24, 25_44, 45_74 disjoint slices

P01_P29 (psych symptoms), P70_P99 (psych diagnoses), P01_P29ogP70_P99 (combined chapter P — exclude from disjoint sums), K70_K99 (cardiovascular), L01_L29 / L70_L99 (musculoskeletal), Skader (injuries), plus specific symptom clusters.
RATE (per-1000 contact rate — only value Atlas ingests). TELLER / SMR / MEIS available upstream.

citation.text: Folkehelseinstituttet. (2024). KPR_1. Retrieved from https://statistikk.fhi.no/nokkel/FEh3FmY9SjEIMKlfUdTVsY9Qe8bwZpCq4IGSRgB9-ag?GEO=0,03&AAR=2020_2020,2021_2021,2022_2022,2023_2023,2024_2024&KJONN=0&ALDER=0_74,15_24&KODEGRUPPE=P01_P29ogP70_P99,P01_P29,P70_P99&MEASURE_TYPE=MEIS. Available in Atlas at https://atlas.sovereignsky.no/datasets/fhi-kpr-1aar.

consuming_marts.title: Latest indicator values per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each
indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner. Backs the
data explorer's per-indicator detail page (atlas-frontend
/data/[source_id]/[contents_code]) and is the equivalent of the
loadIndicatorValues() inline query.

🔴 ROW COUNT IS NOT COVERAGE. A row exists for every active kommune
the source publishes at all, INCLUDING those where `value` is null.
So a series returns ~357 rows whether 357 kommuner have a number or
66 do, and counting rows overstates coverage by up to five times.

⚠️ This has always been true and became dangerous on 2026-09-21,
when nine Ungdata sources published at 18-43 % kommune coverage
against SSB register sources at nearly 100 %. `fhi-hasj` returns
357 rows carrying 66 values.

✅ `indicator_summary.kommuner_with_value` is the live count and the
only thing to trust. It is not restated here on purpose — a number
copied into a description goes stale, which is the defect that made
`fhi-depresjon` advertise fourteen years of data it never held.

PostgREST consumers filter via
?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. The full table is the
cross-product of every indicator with every active kommune that
has a row at latest_year, so the unfiltered row count is large
(~360 active kommuner × ~70 indicators in v1).

Inactive kommuner (kommune_is_active = false) are excluded so the
output reflects today's kommune set, not historical codes that
upstream still emits.

consuming_marts.title: Indicator coverage gaps per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: 🔴 A ROW HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LOW NEED.
consuming_marts.description_full:
🔴 A ROW HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LOW NEED. For `fhi-*` sources it is
usually FHI's disclosure suppression: it hides numbers based on fewer
than ~6 cases, and hides a whole series when more than 20% of it is
hidden, "for ikke å skape et skjevt inntrykk av situasjonen i
kommunen" — to avoid a skewed impression of that kommune.

⚠️ Measured: 105 kommuner are missing from 10+ `fhi-*` series, median
population 1,452, monotonic in population, and EVERY kommune is absent
from at least three. Treating absence as zero in a ranked index
inverts the signal for the smallest kommuner (urb-agents #1379). See

One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) for every
active kommune that has *no* non-NULL value at the indicator's
latest_year. The "coverage gap" sidebar on the data explorer
detail page; equivalent to the listMissingKommuner() inline query.

PostgREST consumers filter via
?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. Membership semantics: a
kommune is considered "missing" if it either has no row at
latest_year, or has a row with value IS NULL. Status markers (':',
'X') do not count as a value.

active kommune that lacks data. Most cells are present, so the
unfiltered row count is the per-indicator gap-list aggregated
across all indicators.

vanish silently. One smuggles the remainder in as a row, the other
discards it, and a consumer summing either gets a number that is
wrong in a direction it cannot see (urb-agents #700, #1250, #1265).

here, named, so reconciling to a national total is a deliberate

change. `is_sentinel` remains a stopgap and this view does not
make the trap gone.

this emits 0 rather than omitting the row: "we checked, none" and
"nobody checked" are different answers, and a missing row cannot
tell them apart.

rather than the parts, which is the thing that was missing: every

consuming_marts.title: Latest indicator values per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner.
consuming_marts.description_full:
One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) at each
indicator's latest_year, restricted to active kommuner. Backs the
data explorer's per-indicator detail page (atlas-frontend
/data/[source_id]/[contents_code]) and is the equivalent of the
loadIndicatorValues() inline query.

🔴 ROW COUNT IS NOT COVERAGE. A row exists for every active kommune
the source publishes at all, INCLUDING those where `value` is null.
So a series returns ~357 rows whether 357 kommuner have a number or
66 do, and counting rows overstates coverage by up to five times.

⚠️ This has always been true and became dangerous on 2026-09-21,
when nine Ungdata sources published at 18-43 % kommune coverage
against SSB register sources at nearly 100 %. `fhi-hasj` returns
357 rows carrying 66 values.

✅ `indicator_summary.kommuner_with_value` is the live count and the
only thing to trust. It is not restated here on purpose — a number
copied into a description goes stale, which is the defect that made
`fhi-depresjon` advertise fourteen years of data it never held.

PostgREST consumers filter via
?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. The full table is the
cross-product of every indicator with every active kommune that
has a row at latest_year, so the unfiltered row count is large
(~360 active kommuner × ~70 indicators in v1).

Inactive kommuner (kommune_is_active = false) are excluded so the
output reflects today's kommune set, not historical codes that
upstream still emits.

consuming_marts.title: Indicator coverage gaps per kommune
consuming_marts.description_short: 🔴 A ROW HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LOW NEED.
consuming_marts.description_full:
🔴 A ROW HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LOW NEED. For `fhi-*` sources it is
usually FHI's disclosure suppression: it hides numbers based on fewer
than ~6 cases, and hides a whole series when more than 20% of it is
hidden, "for ikke å skape et skjevt inntrykk av situasjonen i
kommunen" — to avoid a skewed impression of that kommune.

⚠️ Measured: 105 kommuner are missing from 10+ `fhi-*` series, median
population 1,452, monotonic in population, and EVERY kommune is absent
from at least three. Treating absence as zero in a ranked index
inverts the signal for the smallest kommuner (urb-agents #1379). See
`indicator_summary.kommuners_with_null`.

One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) for every
active kommune that has *no* non-NULL value at the indicator's
latest_year. The "coverage gap" sidebar on the data explorer
detail page; equivalent to the listMissingKommuner() inline query.

PostgREST consumers filter via
?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. Membership semantics: a
kommune is considered "missing" if it either has no row at
latest_year, or has a row with value IS NULL. Status markers (':',
'X') do not count as a value.

The full table is the cross-product of every indicator with every
active kommune that lacks data. Most cells are present, so the
unfiltered row count is the per-indicator gap-list aggregated
across all indicators.

make the trap gone.

tell them apart.

vanish silently. One smuggles the remainder in as a row, the other
discards it, and a consumer summing either gets a number that is
wrong in a direction it cannot see (urb-agents #700, #1250, #1265).

here, named, so reconciling to a national total is a deliberate
act rather than an accident of whether a sentinel survived a

warning — and it is deliberately not bundled with an additive
change. `is_sentinel` remains a stopgap and this view does not
make the trap gone.

this emits 0 rather than omitting the row: "we checked, none" and
"nobody checked" are different answers, and a missing row cannot
tell them apart.

relation and adding every `unattributed_value` for it must equal

    no_kommune_nr         7 489
    kommune_nr_not_current   43
    ---------------------------
    total_value          72 802

7 532 and the 43 Svalbard organisations were counted by neither
relation — silent, self-consistent, and visible only by doing the
subtraction this view exists to support. The singular test
`the_remainder_closes_the_total` now asserts the decomposition
rather than the parts, which is the thing that was missing: every
part had a test and the relationship between them had none.

consuming_marts.description_full:

only thing to trust. It is not restated here on purpose — a number
copied into a description goes stale, which is the defect that made

?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. The full table is the
cross-product of every indicator with every active kommune that
has a row at latest_year, so the unfiltered row count is large
(~360 active kommuner × ~70 indicators in v1).

output reflects today's kommune set, not historical codes that
upstream still emits.
